text:
mike_infra: FYI rolled BMC firmware v2.1.8 to ap-south1 at 00:10 UTC. hitting serial PTY saturation on many racks, provisioning jobs are queuing and GPU allocations are stalling.

olivia_sre: seeing the same from jump hosts — serial consoles are spitting long repetitive logs, pty backlog jumps to 95% and OOB mux starts dropping sessions. GPU pool ap-south1 shows ~18 nodes in 'degraded' pending reprovision.

deploy-bot: firmware-rollout v2.1.8 completed for 42 hosts in ap-south1 (2023-11-02T00:12:00Z)

ben_platform: pasting a snippet of what pty logs look like from one host:
```
[    5.123456] Console: switching to colour frame buffer device 128x48
[    5.124567] bmc-pty0: repeated watchdog dump: nvme0: AER err 0x1
[    5.124568] bmc-pty0: serial line flood: repeated kernel oops header...
```

nidhi: quick cost note: provisioning churn + retries are causing scheduler reschedules; estimate ~10-15% throughput drop for ap-south1 and an incremental burn of ~$3-5k/day if this persists. we should triage fast.

raj_oncall: can we confirm if this is firmware log verbosity change or a pty driver regression? any kernel params flipped?

mike_infra: early hypothesis = firmware enabled verbose console logging on BMC serial multiplexers by default. that pushes huge bursts to host serial ports which back up OOB proxy and cause our provisioner to retry. not seeing kernel parameter flips on hosts yet.

olivia_sre: ran `oobctl pty-stats` on a jammed jump host, shows avg backlog 93% and avg write-q depth ~4k chars/s. also saw `pty: no free pty` messages in the jump host journal.

ben_platform: (suggestion) short-term mitigation: 1) pause rollout for remaining regions/hosts, 2) apply rate-limit on serial output in BMC if firmware supports it, or flip console to lower verbosity. long-term: vendor firmware patch to change default log level or add flood protection.

mike_infra: paused the rest of the rollout (ap-south1 remaining hosts flagged). opening incident and paged vendor contacts.

raj_oncall: can we do a quick experiment on one rack: remote into BMC, set `console.log_level=warning` (if present) and see if pty backlog clears? If that works we can script for rollout pause->update->resume.

olivia_sre: ran that on rack-r17: set log level to warning via IPMI console override, pty backlog dropped to 12% within 40s and provisioner dequeued jobs. good signal.

nidhi: great — runbook impact: mark ap-south1 capacity as partially degraded, notify sales/cc that some Dedicated pools are impacted and to expect slower allocation. cost projection updated to worst-case $6k/day if rollback takes >48h.

ben_platform: temp patch plan: 1) vendor quicksetting change to reduce serial verbosity (tested on r17), 2) throttle provisioner concurrency for ap-south1 to avoid thrashing, 3) schedule full firmware rollback or vendor patch once we have signed build.

mike_infra: action items assigned: mike_infra will coordinate vendor comms and test on 3 more racks; olivia_sre will script the log-level flip for safe rollouts; raj_oncall will throttle provisioner jobs to 10 concurrent; ben_platform will update kms for keystore rotations if needed during patch; nidhi will draft external notice.

olivia_sre: temp script (example):
```bash
# flip BMC console verbosity (tested)
oobctl --host $BMC_IP set-verbosity warning || ipmitool -H $BMC_IP -U admin -P **** raw 0x30 0x45 0x01 0x02
```

raj_oncall: throttled provisioner concurrency for ap-south1 to 10. monitoring scheduler.

mike_infra: vendor engaged, they confirmed a release candidate to disable serial flood by default. asked for signed build and CVE/Change notes.

nidhi: please add a short blurb for ops->customers channel once we have confirmed stable capacity numbers. avoid technical details, flag expected ETA.

ben_platform: note for postmortem - consider adding pty saturation alerts to our console-metrics (pty-backlog > 80% for 2m) and an automated slow-roll policy when OOB error-rate climbs.

mike_infra: will create the incident and link the runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4298. continuing testing on 3 more racks now. will update in 15m. :thumbsup:
